title: REST API Design
summary: Designs or reviews HTTP APIs: resource names, methods, status codes, pagination, error format and versioning, with a short spec before any code.
description: An API outlives the code behind it, so mistakes in names, status codes and error shapes stay for years. This skill makes the agent settle the contract first, in a few lines you can read, and only then write handlers.
It also reviews an existing API against the same checklist and lists the changes that would break clients so they can be planned instead of discovered.
useWhen: Adding a new endpoint or a whole new resource
Reviewing a pull request that changes responses
Clients complain about inconsistent errors or paging
Planning a v2 and deciding what must not break
body:
# REST API design

Settle the contract before writing handlers.

## Steps

1. Read the existing API first: naming, casing, auth, error format, pagination. Match it unless asked to change it.
2. Model resources as plural nouns: `GET /orders`, `GET /orders/{id}`, `POST /orders`, `PATCH /orders/{id}`, `DELETE /orders/{id}`. Nest only one level (`/orders/{id}/items`). Actions that fit no resource get a sub-resource verb (`POST /orders/{id}/cancel`).
3. Use methods correctly: GET and DELETE are safe to retry, PUT replaces, PATCH changes fields, POST creates. Make POST retry-safe with an `Idempotency-Key` header for payments or anything with side effects.
4. Return precise status codes: 200, 201 with `Location`, 204, 400 malformed, 401 not logged in, 403 not allowed, 404, 409 conflict, 422 invalid fields, 429 with `Retry-After`. Never 200 with an error in the body.
5. Use one error shape everywhere: `{"error":{"code":"out_of_stock","message":"...","fields":[{"name":"qty","issue":"..."}]}}`. The code is stable and machine-readable.
6. Paginate every list: cursor-based (`?limit=50&cursor=...`) with a hard maximum and a `next` cursor. Filter and sort with named query params.
7. Version in the path (`/v1`) and only for breaking changes. Adding optional fields is not breaking; removing, renaming or changing a type is.
8. Write the spec (OpenAPI or a table) and get it confirmed before implementing.

## Report

The endpoint table, an example request and response for each, and a list of breaking changes with a migration path.

example.result: POST /v1/teams/{id}/invitations (201, Location), GET same path (cursor paged, max 100), DELETE /v1/invitations/{id} (204), POST /v1/invitations/{id}/accept. Errors: 409 already_member, 422 invalid_email, 429 on more than 20 invites per hour. Not breaking: adding "expires_at" to the response. Spec saved in docs/openapi.yaml.

faq.question: Does it insist on pure REST?
faq.answer: No. It follows the conventions already in your API and uses plain HTTP semantics where they help. Verb sub-resources are fine for actions that are not CRUD.

faq.question: Why cursors rather than page numbers?
faq.answer: Page numbers skip or repeat rows when data changes between requests, and deep offsets get slow. A cursor stays correct and cheap.

access: Writes spec files and handlers when you approve the contract
